title: Patch: the online 1v1 board names the opponent's hero by username, as the daily board and the match's replay already do
thread:
**Issue #3933 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3933: Patch: the online 1v1 board names the opponent's hero by username, as the daily board and the match's replay already do
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

In an online match the label under the opponent's portrait says “Opponent”, though the bar above the board already says who they are (“alice vs Bob#12”). Watch the replay of that same match and the portrait reads “Bob#12”; a daily game's board names the opponent too, and a practice game names the AI and its difficulty. Once this is built, the live board reads the opponent's username under their portrait, falling back to “Opponent” until the names have loaded.

## Why

- `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx:434-445`: the opponent's username is worked out from the ranks read (`useMatchRanks`, `:175-205`) only in the replay branch, where it becomes the replay's `opponentLabel` (#3698).
- The live `<Game>` (`match.tsx:494` on) passes no `enemyLabel`, so `apps/web/src/game/Hero.tsx:229` falls back to `t("Opponent")`.
- The same ranks read already draws both names in the match bar (`match.tsx:606-618`), so nothing new reaches the client: only the hero does not use the name.
- The daily board passes `enemyLabel={game.opponent.username}` (`daily/DailyBoard.tsx:210`) and practice its AI label (`routes/practice.tsx:1037,1119`). R3855000 gave the daily board its opponent's name because “the board's information is the same at every table”, and the live 1v1 table is the one still without it.

## Proposal

- In `match.tsx`, lift the opponent's name (the other seat's username from the ranks read, none when it has not come or is empty) above the replay branch.
- Pass it to the live `<Game>` as `enemyLabel`; with no name, pass nothing, so the hero keeps reading Opponent.
- Leave the modifier list's You and Opponent headings as they are, as R3855000 keeps them on the daily board, and leave a watched game's labels alone (the watch screen has its own).

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`, `apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx`
- SPEC §10.10 (the client's board); a ruling in the issue's block if the bot finds the spec silent on the live hero's label

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In a live online match whose ranks read names the opponent Bob#12, the opponent hero's seat label reads Bob#12 and the viewer's own still reads You.
- [ ] With no ranks read yet, or an empty username, it reads Opponent; the existing R169 tests in `match.test.tsx` keep passing.
- [ ] The finished match's replay still names the opponent (the #3698 test is unchanged).
- [ ] The new test fails without the change, and `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/match.test.tsx` passes.

## Size and risks

Tiny: a few lines in one route and one test. Difficulty medium. Low risk: the name is already on the screen, so CLAUDE.md rule 7 is untouched.

---

## Plan

_Written by `claude-8` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43756479494)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

In a live online 1v1 match, the opponent hero's seat label shows the opponent's username from the ranks read (`Bob#12`). It falls back to `Opponent` when the ranks read has not come or the username is empty. The viewer's own label stays `You`.

The finished match's replay (#3698), the modifier list's You/Opponent headings and the watch screen's labels do not change. The existing R169 and #3698 tests keep passing, and a new test fails without the change.

The spec is silent on the live 1v1 hero's label. R3855000 settled the daily board with the reason "the board's information is the same at every table". So this adds a new ruling, R3933000, as the issue allows.

## Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx` | `change`: compute `opponentName` once, before the replay branch. Reuse it for the replay's `opponentLabel`. Pass it to the live `<Game>` as `enemyLabel`. |
| `apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx` | `change`: add tests named `R3933000 …` in a new `describe`. |
| `spec/rulings/R3933000.md` | `new`: the ruling note, with `proven_in: apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx`. |
| `spec/pending/3933.md` | `new`: the §11 paragraph for R3933000. The `spec/pending/` directory does not exist yet, so create it. |
| `spec/10-engine-guide.md` | `change`: one sentence in the §10.10 hero paragraph (the line starting "The hero each seat plays is a portrait") linking `[[R3933000]]`. |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, any crate, `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md` or `spec/CARDS.md`. Never run `cargo jackioh spec index` or `spec fold`. Leave `apps/web/src/game/Hero.tsx`, `Game.tsx` and `Board.tsx` alone: `enemyLabel` already flows `Game` → `Board` → `heroLabel`/`seatLabel` (`Game.tsx:182,307,1011`, `Board.tsx:732`, `Hero.tsx:229`).

Governing text: §10.10, R3855000 (the daily board's opponent name), R169 (modifier headings stay), R3698/#3698 (replay label, a code comment only, no ruling note), and CLAUDE.md rules 3 and 7.

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`: lift the name.**
   - In `MatchRoute`, `const opponentSeat…` and `const opponentName…` sit at lines ~436-437, inside `if (watching !== null && view.result !== null)`.
   - Move those two lines, with their comment updated, to just after `const over = …` (~line 432) and before that `if`. They sit after all the early returns, so no hook-order problem arises.
   - Keep the code exactly:
     ```ts
     const opponentSeat = ranks === null ? undefined : [ranks.seats.p1, ranks.seats.p2].find((seat) => !seat.you);
     const opponentName = opponentSeat === undefined || opponentSeat.username === "" ? undefined : opponentSeat.username;
     ```
   - New comment: `// #3698, R3933000: the live board's opponent hero and the replay name the other side as the ranks read does, when it has come and holds a name.`
   - The replay branch keeps `{...(opponentName === undefined ? {} : { opponentLabel: opponentName })}` unchanged.

2. **`apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`: pass it to the live board.**
   - In `const board = (<Game …>)` (~line 495), add after `trackStats` (or beside `wearCosmetics`):
     `{...(opponentName === undefined ? {} : { enemyLabel: opponentName })}`
   - Use this spread form, not `enemyLabel={opponentName}`, because the project uses `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` elsewhere. The replay branch uses the same form. With no name, nothing is passed and the hero reads `Opponent`.
   - Do not change `<ModifierList opponentLabel={t("Opponent")} />`.

3. **`spec/rulings/R3933000.md`.** Copy the layout of `spec/rulings/R3855000.md`.
   - Frontmatter: `id: R3933000`.
   - `title: "The online 1v1 board's opponent hero reads the opponent's username, as the daily board's and the match's replay's do (issue #3933; extends R3855000)"`.
   - `cards: "§10.10, R169, R3855000, issue #3933"`.
   - `proven_in:` the list holding `apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx`.
   - Body, short:
     - The live `MatchRoute` board passes `<Game>` the other seat's username from the ranks read (`GET …/ranks`, R604). The same read draws the match bar, so no new information reaches the client (rule 7).
     - Until the read has come, or when the name is empty, the hero reads Opponent.
     - The viewer's seat still reads You. The modifier list's You/Opponent headings stay ([[R169]], [[R3855000]]). A watched game's labels stay as the watch screen has them.
     - "Hearthstone semantics: the board's information is the same at every table."
     - Rejected: also renaming the modifier list's headings, which R3855000 kept; a new endpoint or a name on the view, since the ranks read already holds it.

4. **`spec/pending/3933.md`.** Create the directory and file. One paragraph, in the form `**[[R3933000]] <title> (issue #3933, 2026-11-15)**: <one-paragraph summary of step 3>.` Use the pending files' style, for example `**[[R3954000]] The private lobby's … (issue #3954, 2026-11-15)**: …`.

5. **`spec/10-engine-guide.md`, §10.10 hero paragraph** (the line starting "The hero each seat plays is a portrait ([[R641]])…"). Append one sentence at the paragraph's end, after "…previews the whole pool of twenty-four as they play in a match.": `At an online 1v1 table, a daily game's and a replay of either, the opponent's hero reads the opponent's username once the ranks read has named it, Opponent before ([[R3855000]], [[R3933000]]).` Use a minimal `Edit` with a unique `old_string` taken from the paragraph's last sentence.

6. **`apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx`: tests.** Add a new `describe("R3933000 the online board's opponent hero", …)` after the `R169` describe, or next to the ranks describe at ~line 624. Reuse `render`, `attach`, `socketFactory`, `matchTestid`, `ranksBody` and `stubFetch`. `ranksBody` and `stubFetch` are local to the ranks describe at lines 628-660. Either place the new describe inside it, or copy its shape: a `fetch` stub that answers `/ranks` with the body and anything else with `{ version: "v1", defs: {} }`.
   - Use the same body shape as the #3698 test at ~line 1762: `{ ranked: false, seats: { p1: { profileId: "id-1", username: "Max#3", rank: {…}, you: true }, p2: { profileId: "id-2", username: "Bob#12", rank: {…}, you: false } } }`.

## Tests

File: `apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx`. Each test renders `<MatchRoute matchId="m-1" token="tok" socketFactory={socketFactory} />` and calls `attach()` (viewer `p1`).

- `it("R3933000 the live opponent hero reads the opponent's username and your own still reads You", …)`
  - Stub the ranks as above, then `await screen.findByTestId(matchTestid.ranks)`.
  - Assert `screen.getByTestId("hero-opponent").querySelector(".hero-seat")` has text `Bob#12`.
  - Assert `screen.getByTestId("hero-you").querySelector(".hero-seat")` has text `You`.
  - First check the `hero-you` testid exists with `rg 'hero-you|hero-opponent' apps/web/src/game`. `hero-opponent` is used by the #3698 test. Use whatever `testid` constant `Hero.tsx` uses for the viewer's seat.
- `it("R3933000 with no ranks read yet the opponent hero reads Opponent", …)`
  - Stub fetch so `/ranks` rejects or never resolves. `getMatchRanks` failing leaves `ranks` null: `() => undefined` is the error handler.
  - Render, `attach()`, and assert immediately that the `.hero-seat` of `hero-opponent` reads `Opponent`.
- `it("R3933000 an empty username reads Opponent", …)`
  - Ranks body with `p2.username: ""`.
  - Check what `asMatchRanks` accepts for `username` (`match.tsx` ~lines 140-167). If an empty string is rejected as "not a ranks body", the result is the same: `Opponent`, with no banner. Then assert `findByTestId(matchTestid.ranks)` is present only if the body is accepted. Otherwise wait for the `/ranks` fetch with `waitFor(() => expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.stringContaining("/ranks"), expect.anything()))` before asserting `Opponent`, as the R1436 test at ~line 723 does.

Confirm the first test fails without the change: run it once with step 2 undone, or reason that `Hero.tsx:229` falls back to `Opponent` with no `enemyLabel`. Keep the existing tests unchanged, including the "#3698 the match's replay names the opponent" test and the R169 describe.

Commands, in order:
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/match.test.tsx`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx`
- `cargo jackioh spec check`
- `cargo fmt --check`

## Done when

- [ ] A live match with the opponent named `Bob#12` shows `Bob#12` under the opponent's portrait, and the viewer's label reads `You`.
- [ ] With no ranks read yet, or an empty username, the label reads `Opponent`.
- [ ] The replay still names the opponent (the #3698 test is unchanged and green), the R169 tests are green and the modifier list's headings are unchanged.
- [ ] The new `R3933000` tests pass and fail without the change, and `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/match.test.tsx` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and eslint on the two files are clean.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` passes. The ruling note, its `proven_in` test names, `spec/pending/3933.md` and the §10.10 link are all in place.
- [ ] The harness's checks are green: `cargo fmt --check`, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests and web tests. No change touches the crates, so `apps/web/src/wire` stays unmodified.
- [ ] The decisions are recorded: a new ruling R3933000 rather than a bare change, and the daily board's precedent reused.

## Risks

- **Hidden information (rule 7):** none. The name already renders in the match bar from the same ranks read, and the label is presentation only.
- **Spec check:** `cargo jackioh spec check` fails if an `R3933000` test name has no note, or the note's `proven_in` file holds no test named after it. Name every new test `R3933000 …` and list `match.test.tsx` in the note. `spec/pending/` files must be named `<n>.md` (`3933.md`) and be non-empty.
- **Hook order:** the lifted lines must stay after the early returns and before `if (watching …)`. They use no hooks.
- **Typecheck:** use the conditional spread, not `enemyLabel={opponentName}` with a possibly undefined value.
- **Race:** the ranks read is async, so `Opponent` shows first and the name appears when the read lands, as the match bar does. A test that asserts the name must `await` the ranks banner first.
- **Spec drift:** do not edit `spec/11-rulings.md`, `INDEX.md` or `CARDS.md`; the daily fold writes them.

## Open questions

None. The one non-obvious call, a new ruling rather than citing R3855000 alone, follows the issue's own "a ruling … if the spec is silent" line.
````
